newsitem.title: FRANCE: Veteran French Africa hand Foccart dies at 83.
newsitem.headline: Veteran French Africa hand Foccart dies at 83.

text.p: Veteran French Africa hand Jacques Foccart, who pulled strings on the continent for president Charles de Gaulle and most of his successors, died at his Paris home on Wednesday, an aide said. He was 83.
"We found him dead at the end of the night. I think it was heart failure," his faithful collaborator, Fernand Wibaux, told Reuters from Foccart's home. He had long been ill with Parkinson's disease.

Foccart, who controlled a network of agents across Africa for most of the last 40 years, making and breaking regimes to serve French political and commercial interests, returned to the Elysee palace in 1995 as an honorary adviser to President Jacques Chirac.
After joining De Gaulle in the anti-Nazi French Resistance during World War Two, Foccart became the president's spymaster when he took power in 1958.

Always a secretive and controversial figure, he was accused of conducting a parallel African policy in the 1990s that benefitted old French cronies and contradicted Paris' official support for economic and democratic reforms.
